- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak or adjust downward by 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates drop; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast for next 7–14 days.
- If model forecast mean is significantly higher than recent 18-day average, apply mean reversion correction: subtract 10–20% of forecast gap from next 3–5 days.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values or apply 1–2% downward adjustment.
- If sentiment spikes to 1.00 and model forecasts rise sharply, expect short-term correction; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–7 days unless confirmed by new data.
